answer: Falcon-window arrival ordering. Each new identity must submit its first three actions as a spaced burst: gaps of at least one median network round, with the burst shaped like an orchard row—evenly staggered, no two actions within the same slot. A sonnet-rhythm check rejects bursts whose inter-arrival variance falls below threshold. Attackers must either pay real wall-clock delay per clone, serializing creation across the whole fleet, or pad traffic with idle slots that raise per-identity infrastructure cost.
